questions.question: If the price of 10 notebooks is equal to the price of 4 pens, what is the ratio of the price of a notebook to a pen?
questions.solution:
According to the question, the **price** of **10 notebooks** is equal to the **price** of **4 pens**.

**Calculation:**

Let the price of one **notebook** be **N**

Let the price of one **pen** be **P**

As per the given information:

10 × N = 4 × P

To find the **ratio** of the price of a **notebook** to a **pen** (N : P), we rearrange the equation:

N / P = 4 / 10

Now, simplify the fraction by dividing both the numerator and the denominator by their **common factor** (2):

N / P = 2 / 5

The **ratio** of the price of a **notebook** to the price of a **pen** is **2 : 5**.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 3".**

questions.question: At what time (approximately) (in AM) between 1 AM and 2 AM will the hour and minute hands of the clock overlap?
questions.solution:
__**Concept:**__

The **hour hand** covers 360° in **12 hours**.

Angular distance covered in 1 hour = 360/12 = 30°

Angular distance covered in **60 minutes** = 30°

Angular distance covered in 1 minute = 30/60 = 1/2° (or 0.5°)

The **minute hand** covers 360° in **60 minutes**.

Angular distance covered in 1 minute = 360/60 = 6°

**Relative speed** between the hands = 6° − 0.5° = 5.5° per minute.

**__Calculation:__**

At **1 AM**, the **hour hand** is at the 1 o'clock mark (30°) and the **minute hand** is at the 12 o'clock mark (0°).

The **initial gap** between the hands is 30°.

For the hands to **overlap**, the **minute hand** must gain 30° over the **hour hand**.

Time required = Initial Gap ÷ Relative Speed

Time = 30 ÷ 5.5

Time = 300/55 = 60/11 minutes

Time ≈ 5.45 minutes

Therefore, the hands will overlap at approximately 5.45 minutes past 1, which is **1:05** (approximately).

Hence, the correct answer is **1:05**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

The angle between the **hour hand** and **minute hand** is given by the formula:

Angle (θ) = |30H − (11/2)M|

For the hands to **overlap**, the angle θ must be 0°.

Given **H = 1** (time is between 1 AM and 2 AM).

0 = |30 × 1 − (11/2)M|

30 = (11/2)M

M = 60/11

M ≈ 5.45 minutes

The approximate time is **1:05**.

Therefore, the correct answer is **1:05**.

questions.question: Who is known as the "father of microbiology"?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Antonie van Leeuwenhoek**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Antonie van Leeuwenhoek** (1632−1723) is universally recognized as the **Father of Microbiology** because he was the first person to observe and describe **microorganisms**.
 
• A **Dutch** scientist and businessman, he developed high-quality **single-lens microscopes** with magnification power exceeding **200 times**, which was far superior to the compound microscopes of the **17th century**.
 
• In **1674**, he discovered **protozoa**, and in **1676**, he became the first human to witness **bacteria**, which he initially described as **animalcules** in his letters to the **Royal Society of London**.
 
• His extensive research provided the first microscopic descriptions of **red blood cells**, **spermatozoa**, **yeast**, and the **capillary system**, effectively establishing the foundation for **microbiology** and **protozoology**.
 
• Unlike his contemporaries, Leeuwenhoek achieved exceptional clarity in his lenses, allowing him to visualize the **microscopic world** with a level of detail that would not be surpassed for over a century.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Louis Pasteur**:

 
 
• Commonly referred to as the father of **modern microbiology** and **bacteriology**.
 
• He is famous for proving the **germ theory of disease** and developing the process of **pasteurization** to kill harmful microbes in food.
 
• He created vaccines for **rabies** and **anthrax**, significantly advancing the field of preventive medicine.
 
 
 
• **Robert Hooke**:
 
 
• An English scientist who, in **1665**, used a microscope to observe a thin slice of **cork** and coined the term **cell**.
 
• He published his findings in the landmark book **Micrographia**, which featured detailed illustrations of insects and plants.
 
 
 
• **Edward Jenner**:
 
 
• Regarded as the father of **immunology** for his pioneering work in **1796**.
 
• He developed the **smallpox vaccine**, the first successful vaccine in human history, by utilizing **cowpox** material to create immunity.

questions.question: Which of the following ozone-depleting substances (ODS) releases bromine atoms when exposed to ultraviolet (UV) radiation in the stratosphere?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Halons**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Halons** are a specific class of **halogenated hydrocarbons** that contain **bromine**, along with **fluorine** and **carbon** atoms.
 
• In the Earth's **stratosphere**, these compounds are broken down by high-energy **ultraviolet (UV) radiation** in a process known as **photolysis** or photodissociation.
 
• This reaction results in the release of highly reactive **atomic bromine**, which acts as a powerful catalyst in the destruction of the **ozone layer**.
 
• Scientifically, **bromine** is significantly more destructive to **ozone (O₃)** than chlorine; it is estimated that a single bromine atom can be **40 to 100 times** more efficient at destroying ozone molecules than a single chlorine atom.
 
• Historically, **Halons** were extensively used in **fire suppression systems** and **portable fire extinguishers** because they are electrically non-conductive and leave no residue after application.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Other Ozone-Depleting Substances (ODS):**

 
 
• **Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs):** These contain **chlorine**, fluorine, and carbon. When exposed to UV radiation, they release **chlorine atoms**, which are the primary drivers of ozone depletion in the polar regions.
 
• **Hydrochlorofluorocarbons (HCFCs):** These were developed as transitional substitutes for CFCs. While they also release **chlorine**, they contain **hydrogen**, making them more likely to break down in the lower atmosphere before reaching the stratosphere.
 
• **Carbon tetrachloride (CCl₄):** A heavy, volatile liquid used historically as a **cleaning agent** and **refrigerant precursor**. It releases **chlorine atoms** upon UV exposure and has a high **Ozone Depletion Potential (ODP)**.
 
• **Montreal Protocol:** This 1987 international treaty mandates the phase-out of **Halons** and other ODS to facilitate the recovery of the **Earth's ozone shield**.

questions.question: Which part of the brain is mainly responsible for thinking?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fore-brain**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Fore-brain** (Prosencephalon) is the largest and most complex portion of the human brain, serving as the main site for **higher cognitive functions** and **abstract thinking**.
 
• It includes the **Cerebrum**, which is the specialized region responsible for **logical reasoning**, **intelligence**, **imagination**, and **decision-making**.
 
• The **Cerebral Cortex**, the outer layer of the fore-brain, processes sensory information from the eyes, ears, and skin to translate them into **conscious thoughts** and perceptions.
 
• Within the fore-brain, the **Frontal Lobe** plays a critical role in executive functions such as **problem-solving**, **planning**, and **voluntary muscle control**.
 
• The fore-brain also manages the storage of **long-term memory** and the interpretation of **language**, which are fundamental to the human thinking process.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mid-brain**:

 
 
• Acts as a vital relay center for **visual and auditory impulses** between the hind-brain and fore-brain.
 
• Controls involuntary eye movements and the **pupillary reflex**, which adjusts the size of the pupil in response to light.
 
 
 
• **Hind-brain**:
 
 
• Consists of the **Cerebellum**, **Pons**, and **Medulla Oblongata**.
 
• The **Cerebellum** is responsible for maintaining **posture**, **equilibrium**, and **precision in voluntary movements**.
 
• The **Medulla Oblongata** controls essential life-sustaining involuntary activities like **heartbeat**, **blood pressure**, and **respiration**.
 
 
 
• **Spinal Cord**:
 
 
• A cylindrical bundle of nerve fibers that extends from the **Medulla** through the vertebral column.
 
• It acts as the primary pathway for transmitting signals between the brain and the body and coordinates **reflex actions** without direct brain involvement.

questions.question:
With respect to excretion in Human Beings, which of the following statement is correct?

I. Kidneys are located in the abdomen, one on either side of the backbone. II. Urine produced in the kidneys passes through the ureters into the urinary bladder.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The human **Excretory System** consists of a pair of **kidneys**, which are the primary filtration organs. These **bean-shaped** organs are located in the **abdominal cavity**, positioned retroperitoneally on either side of the **backbone** (vertebral column). *Hence, statement I is correct.*
 
• Once urine is produced in the **nephrons** of the kidneys through processes like **ultrafiltration** and **reabsorption**, it travels down through a pair of long, muscular tubes known as **ureters**. These tubes connect the kidneys to the **urinary bladder**, where urine is stored until it is released. *Hence, statement II is correct.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Components of the Human Urinary System**:

 
 
• **Kidneys**: Responsible for removing **nitrogenous wastes** such as **urea** and **uric acid** from the blood. They maintain **osmoregulation** and **ionic balance**.
 
• **Nephron**: The basic **functional unit** of the kidney. Each kidney contains approximately 1 million nephrons that filter blood to form urine.
 
• **Urinary Bladder**: A distensible muscular organ that acts as a reservoir. It is under the control of the **nervous system**, allowing for voluntary control over **micturition** (urination).
 
• **Urethra**: The final muscular tube through which urine passes from the bladder to the exterior of the body.
 
 
 
• **Blood Supply**: Blood enters the kidneys via the **renal artery** and leaves via the **renal vein** after being filtered.

• **Microorganisms:** These include **Fungi** (molds) and **Bacteria** that cause discoloration, foul odors, and produce toxic substances like **Aflatoxins**.

• **Temperature:** Improper temperatures can lead to **thermal damage** and increase the **respiration rate** of the grains, causing them to lose dry matter.

questions.question: What is the primary function of plant cell wall?

options.text: To carry out photosynthesis in plants

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Provides structural strength to plants**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **plant cell wall** is a specialized, rigid outer layer positioned outside the **cell membrane**, serving as a defining feature of plant cells, fungi, and some algae.
 
• The primary chemical constituent of the cell wall is **cellulose**, a complex **polysaccharide** that provides high tensile and **structural strength** to the plant. Hence, statement 1 is correct.
 
• Because plants lack a skeletal system like animals, the cell wall provides the necessary **rigidity** and framework required for plants to grow tall and resist **mechanical stress**.
 
• It maintains the **shape of the cell** and regulates **turgor pressure**, which is the internal pressure of the cell sap against the wall that keeps the plant **turgid** and upright.
 
• The cell wall acts as a **semi-permeable** barrier that prevents the cell from **osmotic lysis** (bursting) when placed in a **hypotonic environment**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Structural Components**:

 
 
• **Cellulose Microfibrils**: Long chains of **glucose** that form the primary structural skeleton of the wall.
 
• **Hemicellulose and Pectin**: These molecules cross-link cellulose fibers and form the **middle lamella**, acting as a glue between adjacent cells.
 
• **Lignin**: Found in secondary walls, it provides extra **stiffness** and **waterproofing** in woody tissues.
 
 
 
• **Functional Distinctions**:
 
 
• **Photosynthesis and Food Synthesis**: These metabolic functions are carried out by **chloroplasts**, which contain the green pigment **chlorophyll**. The cell wall does not contain the machinery for **carbon fixation**.
 
• **Cell Division**: This process is controlled by the **nucleus** and **cytoskeletal elements** like **microtubules**. While a **cell plate** is formed during cytokinesis to create a new wall, the wall itself does not facilitate the division.

questions.question: Which of the following indices is NOT published by World Economic Forum?

The correct answer is __**Human Development Index**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Human Development Index (HDI)** is a tool developed by the **United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)**, not the **World Economic Forum (WEF)**. It was first introduced in **1990**.
 
• The index was pioneered by Pakistani economist **Mahbub ul Haq** and Indian Nobel laureate **Amartya Sen** to shift the focus of development economics from national income accounting to people-centered policies.
 
• The **HDI** is a composite statistic that aggregates three basic dimensions of human development: **Long and healthy life** (measured by life expectancy at birth), **Knowledge** (measured by mean and expected years of schooling), and a **Decent standard of living** (measured by **GNI per capita** at Purchasing Power Parity).
 
• In contrast, the **World Economic Forum** is an international organization for public-private cooperation based in **Cologny, Switzerland**, and is responsible for the other indices mentioned in the options.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Global Gender Gap Index**:

 
 
• This index was first published in **2006** by the **World Economic Forum**.
 
• It benchmarks national gender gaps on **economic participation**, **educational attainment**, **health and survival**, and **political empowerment**.

questions.question: The product of the three consecutive odd numbers is 9177. What is the largest of the three numbers?
questions.solution:

Estimate the **middle number** by calculating the **cube root** of the product: ³√9177 ≈ 20.94.

Identify the **consecutive odd numbers** near 21, which are 19, 21, and 23.

Verify the **unit digit** product: 9 × 1 × 3 = 27 (Last digit 7 matches 9177).

The **largest number** among 19, 21, and 23 is 23.

**∴ The correct answer is 23.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Product of **three consecutive odd numbers** = 9177.

**Formula Used:**

If the **middle number** is x, then the numbers are (x − 2), x, and (x + 2).

Product = (x − 2) × x × (x + 2) = x × (x² − 4) = x³ − 4x.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ab0436b7b6062226a0303da1572c489a538c973c3c0ff9294385b2e2680c250d.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ x³ − 4x = 9177

⇒ We know that 20³ = 8000 and 22³ = 10648.

⇒ Testing **odd number** x = 21:

⇒ 21³ − 4(21) = 9261 − 84 = 9177 (Matches given product).

⇒ The numbers are 19, 21, and 23.

⇒ The **largest** of these numbers is 23.

**∴ The correct answer is 23.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Arithmetic Progression of Odd Numbers

Consecutive odd numbers always have a **common difference (d)** of 2. They can be represented as n, n+2, n+4...

Average of Consecutive Odd Numbers

Properties of Odd Products

The product of any number of odd integers is **always odd**. If the product is even, at least one of the numbers must be even.

questions.question: (380 + 120)² - (380 - 120)² = ?

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

⇒ Expression = [(380 + 120) + (380 − 120)] × [(380 + 120) − (380 − 120)]

⇒ Expression = [380 + 120 + 380 − 120] × [380 + 120 − 380 + 120]

⇒ Expression = [2 × 380] × [2 × 120]

⇒ Expression = 760 × 240

**∴ The correct answer is 760 × 240.**

Standard Squaring Formulas

Difference of Two Squares

⇒ Sum = 42925 − 2870

⇒ Sum = 40055.

**∴ The correct answer is 40055.**

Balance the 2ⁿd number: 10 − 4 = 6 parts.

2 × **First Number** = 6 × **Second Number** ⇒ Ratio = 6 : 2 = 3 : 1.

**∴ The correct answer is 3 : 1.**
